Financial Analyst is an umbrella title with different duties across institutions: corporate financial planning and analysis (FP&A) supports internal budgets and operating decisions; sell-side research involves public disclosures and research reports; buy-side research supports fund managers; quantitative analysis relies on models and data; credit and financial risk analysis focuses on losses and limits; and personal wealth management serves clients within a licensing framework. Before comparing jobs, check clients, output formats (internal support, external research, or investment advice), data and model environments, access to material nonpublic information, compliance and conflict-of-interest requirements, and qualification and disclosure agreements.

Test this through a paper exercise: given an entirely fictional analysis assignment specifying a business question, available financial and market data, compliance and disclosure restrictions, required conclusion formats, and modeling resources, write data checking and definition alignment methods, models and assumptions, scenario and sensitivity plans, statements of conclusions and uncertainty, and review and recordkeeping methods, marking conclusions requiring compliance, risk control, or licensed manager confirmation.

Signals worth considering: willingness to continually check data and definitions, retain multiple scenarios when assumptions are uncertain rather than force one answer, document evidence, and accept independent review. Signals calling for caution: focusing on conclusions without assumptions, treating compliance and conflicts of interest as steps that can be bypassed, and replacing evidence with confident language.
This card is a career exploration reference. It does not constitute a hiring decision, ability rating, investment advice, or legal or compliance conclusion.

First consider whether you are willing to work with data, models, and assumptions over the long term, operate within compliance and conflict-of-interest constraints, and accept review. Test this with this page's paper exercise and seven-day tasks.

Financial analysts' daily work cycles through data extraction, modeling, validation, and explanation: extract usable information from corporate disclosures, accounting records, and industry and market data, checking definitions and time references; build valuation or forecasting models for decision questions and document key assumptions; run baseline, upside, and downside scenarios and sensitivity tests to identify assumptions conclusions are most sensitive to; write research conclusions, valuation ranges, or investment recommendations, explaining assumptions and uncertainty to investment committees, fund managers, or clients; conduct independent review under institutional procedures, maintain model versions, retain evidence, and coordinate with investment, risk, compliance, accounting, and business teams. O*NET also lists securities pricing, fundraising and debt restructuring communication, transaction material preparation, investment purchases under company policy, and guiding junior members. Additional duties depend on business authorization.

subject.name: Financial Analysts
subject.summary: Perform quantitative work on whether to invest, how to value an investment, and where risks lie: extract usable information from corporate disclosures, accounting records, and industry and market data and check definitions; build valuation or forecasting models for decision questions and state assumptions clearly; run baseline, upside, and downside scenarios to identify the assumptions conclusions are most sensitive to; organize results into research conclusions, valuation ranges, or investment recommendations, explaining evidence and uncertainty to investment committees, fund managers, or clients; conduct independent review under institutional compliance procedures, maintain model versions, and retain records; collaborate with investment, risk, compliance, accounting, and business teams; and follow local laws and institutional procedures.
